evidences.title: USA 2-1 Ghana: a nation reacts to the World Cup 2014 game | World Cup 2014 | The Guardian
evidences.content:
Clint Dempsey scored after 29 seconds, Ghana equalised and then John Brooks scored a late winner to delight Jrgen Klinsmann, the huge travelling support and a country that is falling in love with soccer like never before. It was all a bit special How are you supporting your team at the World Cup?

After Iran and Nigeria had the temerity to play out a goalless draw in this World Cup of World Cups, we were due some drama from USA v Ghana. The 22 players, two managers, one president and hundreds of millions of fans involved did not disappoint. Barack Obama made the first move of the night by sending a message of support from the While House. Clint Dempsey took heed, showing his president how to react quickly in a tough international situation by scoring after only 29 seconds.

USA stuttered after their early goal, losing Jozy Altidore to injury and ceding more possession and territory as Ghana began to dictate the play. With only eight minutes left, the inevitable happened. Andr Ayew scored for Ghana.

Ghana had the momentum. Kevin Prince Boateng and Michael Essien were on from the bench and the USA players looked dead on their feet. The game looked to be up for Klinsmann's men, but with 86 minutes on the clock, John Brooks came up for a corner. He had dreamt he would score a late winner in this game, but this sport has a way of turning dreams to dust. He couldn't possibly score his first goal in international football in the USA's opening game at a World Cup, could he? Yes he could.
